question: Which of the following is an example of emulsion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Milk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Milk is an emulsion or colloid of butterfat globules within a water-based fluid that contains dissolved carbohydrates and protein aggregates with minerals.
 
• An emulsion is a mixture of two or more liquids that are normally immiscible (unmixable or unblendable) owing to liquid-liquid phase separation.
 
• Common examples of emulsions include egg yolk, butter, and mayonnaise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
 

 Term
 Description
 
 

 Suspension
 
 
A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture of a fluid that contains solid particles sufficiently large for sedimentation.

 
Examples- Muddy water, Milk of magnesia, Sand particles suspended in water, Flour in water, Slaked lime for whitewashing, etc.

 
 
 

 Gel
 
 
A gel is a colloidal system in which the dispersed phase is liquid and the dispersion medium is solid.

 
Examples - Curd, cheese, butter, etc.

 
 
 

 Foam
 
 
A foam is a dispersion of a gas in a liquid prepared using a foaming agent, which in most cases consists of one or more surfactants.

 
Examples - whipped cream, fire retardant foam, and soap bubbles, etc.
